texts.facts: Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t he PFA Act and Rules. 2. That on 21.3.2001 at about 5.00 PM, Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh Suniti Kumar Gupta purchased sample of 'Sundae Mix', a food article for analysis from accused No.1 Gurmukh Singh from the premises M/s Wimpy International Ltd. N-6, Janpath, Connaught Place, New Delhi, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No. 1 Gurmukh Singh was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted of approx. 900 gms. of 'Sundae Mix' (ready for use) taken from a sealed polythene packet having label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. T.S. Mutty, DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. LHA/SDM(New Delhi). The sample taken in a clean & dry stainless steel container after thoroughly mixing the contents of the packet by shaking the packet while sealed. Again mixed with a clean & dry plastic spoon while in the container. 36 drops of formalin added in each bottle by a clean and dry glass dropper. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and scaled according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Gurmukh and the price of the sample was also given to him vide vendor's receipt dated 21-3-2001. Panchnama was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by Fl were signed by accused No. 1 Gurmukh Singh and the other witness Sh R.K. Bhaskar FI. Before starting sampling proceedings, efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such, Sh. R.K. Bhaskar, FI was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi bearing LHA Code Number TSM/LHA//3657 in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact conditions. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be non-conforming to the standards of Ice cream.. The report of Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample does not conform to the standards because ice cream fat, total solids and protein are less than the prescribed minimum limit of 12%, 36% and 3.5% respectively. The sample has been judged on the standards of ice cream." Da vs Gurmukh Singh Etc. on 6 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180154024/ 2 DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Gurmukh Singh was the vendor-cum-restaurant Manager of accused No. 2 M/s Wimpy International Ltd, N-6, Janpth Connught Place, New Delhi, at the time of sampling. M/s Wimpy International Ltd earlier name was Goodwill Food Pvt Ltd. Accused No.2 M/s Wimpy International Ltd has appointed accused No. 3 Sophia Joseph as Assistant Restaurant Manager as its nominee under Section 17 of the PFA Act. She is treated as valid nominee on the date of sampling. So vendor's restaurant and above nominee are the delinquent party. 5. It is further stated that accused No. 2 M/s Wimpy International Ltd. has purchased the sampled commodity from accused No. 4 M/s Royal Refrigeration (Jay Ice Cream), 13 Thyagraj Nagar Market (Near Lodhi Road), New Delhi-03, vide delivery challan No.9792 dated 21-3-2001. Accused No. 4 M/s Royal Refrigeration (Jay Ice Cream) is a partnership firm as per Sales Tax office, Delhi, ASTO, W-99 reply, and there are two partners i.e. accused No. 5 Balraj Yadav and accused No. 6 Sh. Vinod Kheara, both partners along with firm are liable and responsible for the said business. 6. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.11.2002 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. 7. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 07.11.2002. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. The CFL passed the sample for protein content but failed it in fat and total solids. Notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. During the trial, the accused No. 2 Gurmukh Singh was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 15.10.2009. 8. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 SDM/LHA Sh T.S. Mutty, PW-2 FI Sh Suniti Kumar Gupta, PW-3 FI Sh Bal Mukund and PW-4 FI Sh R.K. Bhaskar. PW-1 and PW-4 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. T.S. Mutty. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the 900 gms sample of Sundae Mix (a kind of Ice cream) from sealed polythene packet from the accused No.1, shaking the sealed packet and then it was taken into stainless steel container, rotating it in all possible directions, several times, divided the sample commodity into three counterparts by putting them into clean and dry glass bottles, adding 36 drops of formalin in each sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in form VI Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Da vs Gurmukh Singh Etc. on 6 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180154024/ 3 Ex.PW-1/C. The vendor furnished source of purchase of sample commodity accordingly notice u/s 14 A Ex.PW1/D addressing to M/s Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream was also prepared at the spot. Thereafter, on the next working day i.e. 22.03.2001, two counterparts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in sealed packet were deposited vide receipt Ex.PW1/E with intimation that one counter of the sample has already been deposited with PA and one counter part was deposited vide PA receipt Ex.PW1/F. Thereafter, PA Report Ex. PW1/G was received, according to which the sample does not conform to the standard. Thereafter, after completion of the investigation, the complete case file along with all the statutory documents was sent to Director Sh K.S. Wahi for obtaining consent for prosecution of accused persons and the then Director, PFA, after applying his mind granted his consent for prosecution Ex.PW1/H and the present complaint Ex. PW1/I was filed before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW3/A along with copy of PA Reports were sent to accused persons through postal receipt Ex.PW3/B. During investigation PW-2 FI Sh Suniti Kumar Gupta received a letter Ex.PW2/C from Jay Ice Cream. During investigation PW-2 sent a letter to Royal Refrigeration Jay ice Cream through registered post Ex.PW-2/D seeking information on the constitution the said firm but no reply was received. Thereafter PW-2 sent a letter to the vendor vide Ex.PW2/E and received its reply Ex. PW 2/E-1 wherein they disclosed that the sample commodity was purchased from M/s Royal Refrigeration vide Delivery Challan No. 9792 dated 21.03.2001. It was also DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. disclosed in the said reply that Ms.Sophia Joseph was the Nominee of Wimpy International Ltd. PW-2 also received documents Mark Y-1 to Mark Y-6. PW-2 also sent a letter to Wimpy international Ltd through registered post vide Ex.PW2/F and received its reply vide Ex.PW 2/F-1 alongwith document mark Y-7. PW-2 also sent a Letter to CMO. NDMC through registered post vide Ex. PW 2/G seeking information on the constitution of Wimpy International Ltd. but, did not receive its reply. PW-2 also sent a letter to DHO, MCD Lajpat Nagar Zone vide Ex. PW 2/G-1 for seeking information on the constitution of Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream and received its reply at portion 'X' stating that Shri Vinod Khera was its Proprietor. Thereafter PW-2 submitted the letter to PFA Department vide Ex. PW 2/H for seeking information on the constitution of Wimpy international Ltd. & Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream and received its reply at portion 'X to X' stating that Ms. Sophia Joseph was the Nominee of Wimpy International Ltd. however. there was no Nomination regarding Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream. PW-2 received a reply vide envelop Ex.PW2/H2 from STO. Ward No. 88 vide Ex. PW 2/H-1 wherein it was disclosed that Wimpy International Ltd. was having 3 Directors, as mentioned therein. Thereafter PW-2 sent a reminder to Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream through registered post vide Ex. PW 2/l but received no reply from them. PW-2 further sent one more letter & reminder through registered post to Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream vide Ex. PW 2/I-1 & Ex.PW 2/I-2 but received no reply. PW-2 also sent a letter to STO Ward No. 99 vide Ex. PW2/J and received its reply at portion 'X to X' stating that M/s Royal Refrigeration was having 2 Partners namely Shri Vinod Khera and Shri Balraj Yadav. PW-2 also sent DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. another Letter to STO Ward No. 99 vide Ex. PW 2/J-1, asking him to supply copy of Partnership Deed of Royal Refrigeration Jay Ice Cream but, they did not supply the copy of partnership deed. The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence counsel. 9. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 27.02.2016 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was fixed for defence evidence. Da vs Gurmukh Singh Etc. on 6 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180154024/ 4 10.In defence , the accused No.3 Ms Sophia Joseph examined herself as DW-1 and placed on record letter Ex.DW1/A wherein she has left the job from Wimpy International Ltd. Thereafter, the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments. 11.The present case alleges adulteration in the sample of "Ice cream Sundae mix" collected from the business concern of the accused no. 1. This sample of ice cream has been analysed twice, firstly by the PA and secondly, by the CFL.
texts.arguments: 12.The prime argument of the Ld. Defence Counsel on the basis of which acquittal is sought at the threshold in this matter is thus, 'since there is variation of more than 0.3% in the reports of PA and CFL, the samples were not representative'. Pointing out the above said variation in the presence of milk fat, total solids and proteins, it is contended that the same would be sufficient to conclude that samples were not taken by the FI in proper manner and were not representative, for which benefit should be given to DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. the accused. 13.In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in State v. Ramesh Chand [2010(2)JCC 1250], Food Inspector v. Parvinder Malik [2014(2) FAC 306], State v. Vinod Kumar Gupta [2010(2) JCC 957], State v. Virender Kohli [2014(2) FAC 223], State v. Kamal Aggarwal [2014(2) FAC 183], State v. Vidya Gupta [2014(1) FAC 291], State v. Dinesh Goswami [2014(1) FAC 302], State v. Mahabir [2014(1) FAC 286], State v. Santosh Sharma [2014(1) FAC 296], Raja Ram Seth & Sons v. Delhi Administration [2012(2) FAC 523], State v. Sunil Dutt [2011(4) JCC 2377] and State v. Rama Rattan Malhotra [2012(2) FAC 398]. 14.As per section 13(3) of the PFA Act, the certificate issued by the Director of CFL shall supersede the report of the PA. As per proviso to section 13(5) of the Act, such certificate shall be final and conclusive evidence for the facts stated therein. 15.In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. therein are concerned. 16.In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under: (a) The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason. (b) Once the Director has examined the sample and has DA vs Gurmukh Singh etc. delivered his certificate, under proviso to sub-section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein.
